\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{আপত্তি} (āpôtti)}{আপত্তি (āpôtti)}]{\bn{আপত্তি} (āpôtti) — an objection}

\label{lesson:BN-C334-apotti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for against, then the Bengali for to back.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{আপত্তি}}
\textbf{\bn{আপত্তি}} — \emph{āpôtti} — \textquotedblleft{}an objection\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{তোমার} \bn{কোনো} \bn{আপত্তি} \bn{আছে}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tomār kono āpôtti āchhe?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Do you have any objection?
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{আপত্তি}} (\emph{āpôtti}) is Sanskrit \emph{āpatti}, something that befalls one, a mishap (Monier-Williams). The Bengali sense, an objection someone raises, is not one the dictionary gives.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āpôtti}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āpôtti}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tomār kono āpôtti āchhe?} — Do you have any objection?
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for against, then the Bengali for to back, then say \emph{āpôtti} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{আপত্তি} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An objection\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বিতর্ক} (bitôrkô)}{বিতর্ক (bitôrkô)}]{\bn{বিতর্ক} (bitôrkô) — a debate}

\label{lesson:BN-C334-bitorko}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to back, then the Bengali for an objection.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বিতর্ক}}
\textbf{\bn{বিতর্ক}} — \emph{bitôrkô} — \textquotedblleft{}a debate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{কাল} \bn{স্কুলে} \bn{একটা} \bn{বিতর্ক} \bn{হবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāl skule ekṭā bitôrkô hôbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There will be a debate at school tomorrow.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বিতর্ক}} (\emph{bitôrkô}) is Sanskrit \emph{vitarka}, a weighing of guesses and doubts (Monier-Williams). Bengali uses it for a formal debate between two sides; that use is modern.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bitôrkô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bitôrkô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāl skule ekṭā bitôrkô hôbe.} — There will be a debate at school tomorrow.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to back, then the Bengali for an objection, then say \emph{bitôrkô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{বিতর্ক} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A debate\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{মতামত} (môtāmôt)}{মতামত (môtāmôt)}]{\bn{মতামত} (môtāmôt) — opinions; views}

\label{lesson:BN-C334-motamot}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for an objection, then the Bengali for a debate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{মতামত}}
\textbf{\bn{মতামত}} — \emph{môtāmôt} — \textquotedblleft{}opinions; views\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{সবার} \bn{মতামত} \bn{শুনে} \bn{আমরা} \bn{সিদ্ধান্ত} \bn{নেব।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sôbār môtāmôt shune āmrā siddhāntô nebô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We will decide after hearing everyone's views.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{মতামত}} (\emph{môtāmôt}) is usually explained as a Bengali pairing of Sanskrit \emph{mata}, an opinion, with \emph{a-mata}, not approved of (both in Monier-Williams), so 'views for and against'; the pair itself is not in the dictionary. It asks for everyone's opinions at once.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{môtāmôt}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{môtāmôt}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sôbār môtāmôt shune āmrā siddhāntô nebô.} — We will decide after hearing everyone's views.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for an objection, then the Bengali for a debate, then say \emph{môtāmôt} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{মতামত} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Opinions; views\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বিরোধিতা} \bn{করা} (birodhitā kôrā)}{বিরোধিতা করা (birodhitā kôrā)}]{\bn{বিরোধিতা} \bn{করা} (birodhitā kôrā) — to oppose}

\label{lesson:BN-C334-birodhita-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a debate, then the Bengali for views.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বিরোধিতা} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{বিরোধিতা} \bn{করা}} — \emph{birodhitā kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to oppose\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{অনেক} \bn{মানুষ} \bn{নতুন} \bn{রাস্তার} \bn{বিরোধিতা} \bn{করল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ônek mānush nôtun rāstār birodhitā kôrlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Many people opposed the new road.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{পরিকল্পনার} \bn{বিরোধিতা} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini pôrikôlpônār birodhitā kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বিরোধিতা} \bn{করা}} (\emph{birodhitā kôrā}) is Sanskrit \emph{virodhitā}, enmity or strife (Monier-Williams), with \bn{করা}. Bengali softened it to open opposition; what is opposed takes -\bn{এর}: \bn{রাস্তার} \bn{বিরোধিতা}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{birodhitā kôrā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{birodhitā kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ônek mānush nôtun rāstār birodhitā kôrlô.} — Many people opposed the new road.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a debate, then the Bengali for views, then say \emph{birodhitā kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{বিরোধিতা} \bn{করা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To oppose\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{উপেক্ষা} \bn{করা} (upekkhā kôrā)}{উপেক্ষা করা (upekkhā kôrā)}]{\bn{উপেক্ষা} \bn{করা} (upekkhā kôrā) — to ignore; to disregard}

\label{lesson:BN-C334-upekkha-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for views, then the Bengali for to oppose.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{উপেক্ষা} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{উপেক্ষা} \bn{করা}} — \emph{upekkhā kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to ignore; to disregard\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{তুমি} \bn{আমার} \bn{আপত্তি} \bn{উপেক্ষা} \bn{করলে} \bn{কেন}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tumi āmār āpôtti upekkhā kôrle ken?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Why did you ignore my objection?
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{আমাদের} \bn{প্রশ্ন} \bn{উপেক্ষা} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini āmāder prôshno upekkhā kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{উপেক্ষা} \bn{করা}} (\emph{upekkhā kôrā}) is Sanskrit \emph{upekṣā}, overlooking or disregard (Monier-Williams), with \bn{করা}. It is a choice not to heed, stronger than not noticing.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{upekkhā kôrā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{upekkhā kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tumi āmār āpôtti upekkhā kôrle ken?} — Why did you ignore my objection?
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for views, then the Bengali for to oppose, then say \emph{upekkhā kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{উপেক্ষা} \bn{করা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To ignore; to disregard\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
